newsitem.title: USA: USDA sees rising meat exports to S.Korea, Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: USDA sees rising meat exports to S.Korea, Bulgaria.

text.p: Demand will improve during the second half of 1997 for U.S. pork exported to South Korea and U.S. beef to Bulgaria, the Agriculture Department said Monday.

In a trade highlights circular published by the Foreign Agricultural Service, the agency said U.S. exports of beef, pork and variety meats in the period from January to April were off by 12 percent, 20 percent and 21 percent, respectively from the year-earlier period.
U.S. exports of dairy products during the four months rose 10 percent, cattle hides and skins were up 12 percent, and poultry rose 5 percent, the USDA said.
U.S. pork exports were off to a strong start this year in South Korea, the report said.

U.S. pork exports to South Korea hit 4.3 million tonnes, up 89 percent, during January through April, the agency said. "Though U.S. exports of pork to Korea were forecast to increase during 1997, this was not expected to occur until after July 1, when Korea's market for frozen pork imports is scheduled to be liberalized," USDA said.
U.S. exporters would also see rising sales to Bulgaria, the report said. Last year, U.S. exports to Bulgaria totaled 121 tonnes of beef, 5 tonnes of pork and 326 tonnes of poultry.

"U.S. red meat and poultry exporters have an excellent opportunity to expand exports to the Bulgarian market, as a result of high prices and declining livestock and poultry production in that country," USDA said. "Beef exporters should benefit most as Bulgaria is consistently short of good quality beef."

USDA said that Egypt was expected to lift a nearly decade-old ban on imports of poultry meat soon, allowing imports at a duty rate of 70 percent. Prior to the 1988 ban, Egypt was a major importer of frozen poultry meat from the United States.
Romania, which used to buy $15-20 million worth of annual poultry meat from U.S. exporters, has lowered duties from 141 percent to 60 percent.

"While trade sources optimistically estimated that Romania could import up to 50,000 (metric) tons of poultry meat this year, it was questionable whether U.S. product could be competitive at those tariff levels," the USDA said.

The report said the hog cholera situation in the Netherlands had worsened. As of June 27, 3 million animals, or nearly one-fourth of all Dutch pigs, had been destroyed at a cost of $523.6 million, the USDA said, and it was unclear how soon officials would get the disease under control.
Brazilian exports of broiler meat during the first four months of 1997 could mean record exports for all of this year, the report said.

Brazil, the second largest exporter of broiler meat after the United States, is expected to export nearly 600,000 tonnes this year, up 40 percent from two years ago. "Relatively stagnant domestic demand for chicken meat has led to an oversupply of product, dropping wholesale bird prices to nearly 38 cents a pound, compared to the current U.S. price of 59 cents a pound," the report said.

Colombia's poultry producers are urging the Colombia government to restrict imports of mechanically deboned chicken, the USDA said. U.S. exporters sold $13.6 million worth of poultry to Colombia last year.
